A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LogicTree study. Their complete main texts, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-dataset experiments, reproduced baseline comparisons, component ablations, and reasoning-step and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds mathematical-reasoning results, token-budget experiments, and token-use and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix H and Figure 11 add a limited arithmetic adaptation: the module workflow selects numerical information, performs arithmetic derivations, reuses intermediate quantities, and produces a numerical answer. The original logical-reasoning DFS, caches, and prioritization components remain. Detailed prompts for the adaptation are not supplied.

E1.justification: v2 retains all five logical-reasoning datasets and adds GSM8K and MathQA evaluations in Appendix H. These introduce mathematical word-problem solving and numerical answers, substantially extending coverage beyond truth-valued logical hypothesis verification.

E2.justification: The main accuracy and ablation comparator sets are unchanged. Resource comparisons expand to include o1-mini and o3-mini in the new token/time table (Table 7), whereas v1 explicitly excluded them from reasoning-step analysis. The mathematical evaluation reuses CoT and ToT.

E3.justification: v2 introduces token-budget sweeps on ProofWriter and RobustLR with GPT-4o, generated-token and inference-time metrics, and mathematical evaluations using Qwen2.5-7B on 300 randomly sampled test examples per dataset. These add substantive evaluation protocols. Existing logical-dataset samples and the 80-query limit remain unchanged; the main-text change from 'step' to 'query' clarifies an existing setting.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds direct analysis of accuracy at matched token budgets, a question not tested by v1's comparisons of average reasoning steps. Table 7 adds resource profiling, and Figure 11 adds a worked mathematical case. Existing prioritization/cache ablations, depth analysis, and error analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 newly states that all results come from a single run. v1 did not disclose the run count. This is additional reporting, not evidence of changed repetition counts; neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing logical-accuracy, ablation, and reasoning-step results are unchanged. New Figure 11 reports GSM8K/MathQA accuracies of 94.3/71.0 for LogicTree, 90.3/64.7 for ToT, and 88.7/60.7 for CoT under the Qwen2.5-7B setup. Figure 9 adds budget-dependent accuracy results, and Table 7 adds token/time measurements. These are new results, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores.

T1.justification: The semantic-overlap weights, cumulative-connectivity definition, and premise-search complexity reasoning are retained. Appendix A revises notation and explains the set representation more explicitly, without introducing a substantive mathematical definition, derivation, or proof change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about structured exploration, caching, linear premise search, prioritization, and inference-time scaling. The headline gains over CoT, ToT, and o3-mini are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 interprets the new budget curves as evidence of more effective computation scaling, and Appendix H discusses broader adaptability. The limitations soften the structured-input qualification and remove the specific warning that prioritization heuristics may fail when sentence structure is unclear, while retaining the explicit-premise requirement.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link, identifies the spaCy model as en_core_web_lg-3.8.0 with its size, and specifies completion_tokens as the source of generated-token counts. These improve access and implementation documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for GSM8K, MathQA, and Qwen2.5 to support the mathematical extension. The main related-work positioning remains unchanged. Updating Cumulative Reasoning from its 2024 reference to its 2025 publication identifies the same work.

P1.justification: There are localized language edits and clarifications in the introduction, module descriptions, limitations, and Appendix A. v2 expands Appendix E, inserts the mathematical extension as Appendix H, moves the existing prompt appendix to I, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the token-budget plots (Figure 9), mathematical case/results display (Figure 11), and resource table (Table 7). Existing appendix figures and tables are rearranged, with small label and caption refinements. The original visual material and general layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The matched-budget curves and token/time table provide more direct evidence for the scaling claim and expose its resource tradeoffs. Mathematical evaluations broaden empirical support, while the code link, model details, and single-run disclosure improve transparency. These benefits outweigh the softened limitation language. However, sparse documentation of the new mathematical and budget protocols, together with absent uncertainty estimates, limits the overall gain.
